newsitem.title: USA: U.S. auditors' independence standards board set up.
newsitem.headline: U.S. auditors' independence standards board set up.

text.p: The Securities and Exchange Commission and American Institute of Certified Public Accountants Monday jointly named eight persons to a board created to set independence standards for auditors.

The new organization, Independence Standards Board, is made up of public and practicing accounting profession members operating under SEC oversight and within the AICPA, the two bodies said in their joint statement.
Chaired by Chancellor William Allen of the Delware Court of Chancery, the ISB is expected to convene for the first time in July at which an executive director will be named.

"Success in clarifying which auditor activities are consistent with the integrity of audited financial statements can contribute to the reliability of financial data and promote informed, efficient capital markets," Allen said.
The board was created in response to rising challenges of addressing auditor independence issues as business and professional relationships have become more complex.

The public members of the board in addition to Allen are John Bogel, chairman of the board, the Vanguard Group Inc; Robert Denham, chairman and chief executive officer, Salomon Inc, and Manuel Johnson, co-chairman and senior partner, Johnson Smick International and former vice-chairman of the board of governors of the Federal Reserve System.

The accounting profession members are are Stephen Butler, chairman and CEO, KPMG Peat Marwick LLP; Philip Laskawy, chairman and CEO, Ernst & Young LLP; Barry Melancon, president and CEO, American Institute of Certified Public Accountants and James Schiro, chairman and senior partner, Price Waterhouse LLP.
